rationale: The landlord approved an engineer (008). The engineer visited and the agency held for his invoice (017, 021). An invoice for GBP 75.11 has now arrived (024); its due date (July 2026) is noise. The agency told the landlord the heating-element wiring had been replaced for '£75 + VAT', then closed after final checks (025-031). Close-out is right, with the landlord told the invoice is £75.11 as shown; the agency's '£75 + VAT' is not the amount on the invoice. Because a contractor call on 27 February (022) asked to schedule a visit after the job was apparently done, confirming the repair with the tenant first is acceptable. The intake label 'Heating & Hot Water' is a misclassification: the property's hot water is unaffected (002). The appliance fault is not the tenant's, and nothing further needs booking.
